gate0.note:
GATE 0: idea-04 Lift. Human decision, stated as 'pick 4'. No rationale was given beyond the choice, and none is invented here.

CARRY TO GATE 1 - the idea's own three stated risks, in its words:
  1. POLICY SPRAWL IS WHAT KILLS THIS. 'Serve calls in passing order' has at
     least three readings, and unless the spec fixes one as an ordered
     procedure the Builder and the Verifier will produce two plausible traces
     and grade different ones. This is the one to watch at Gate 1.
  2. A trace invites over-pinning. Criteria should name the served tick per
     call and the floor at two or three named ticks - NOT assert the whole
     array, or one extra doors tick fails every criterion at once.
  3. nextTarget is the heavy cut. Split it inside session 2 (direction choice
     separate from the pending-ahead test) rather than moving part of it into
     session 1, which already carries the project setup.

BUDGET: 2 x 40 minutes. Six consecutive projects have overrun their session cap;
pipeline-test-04 measured 47 minutes on a 40-minute session in an earlier round
and only reached 40 after a disclosed trim. Session 1 here carries setup plus
step(); session 2 carries nextTarget plus runUntil plus an endpoint.

NEW GROUND: first discrete-time simulation in the track, and the first loop whose
termination is part of the specification (runUntil's guard). Also the first
discriminated union modelling a mode - moving / doors / idle - rather than a
success/failure result.

gate1.note:
GATE 1 APPROVED - round 2. Human decision. The stopping rule was approve-eligible
on its own; no --override.

RULE: 1 blocking finding, owned by test-runner; 12 worth a look; 0 blocking
findings owned by 'nothing'. Linter 0 errors / 0 warnings, first try both rounds.
Drift against round 1: none. Sessions 39.3 / 36.5 against the 40 cap. 12
criteria, 5 cuts, pairwise distinct signatures.

ROUND 1's TWO MUST-FIX ITEMS ARE FIXED, AND THE FIXES WERE VERIFIED TO BITE
rather than taken on trust - the Breaker re-derived the wrong implementation's
output by hand:
  - B1: with `overtake` seeded floor 5 before floor 8, `ahead = live` targets
    floor 5 from floor 6 at tick 2, so c-2-2's tick-2 row reads `down` and goes
    red. With `both-sides` seeded floor 6 before floor 2, the same reading swaps
    c-2-1's servedAt values and goes red.
  - B2: c-2-2's new tick-5 floor-8 `direction: down` row is the only
    downward-moving car any criterion observes, so `direction: 'up'`
    unconditionally is now red.
All four runUntil traces and the five-click `above` walk were re-derived against
the new seed order; every pinned row, servedAt and row count reproduces.

THE ONE BLOCKING FINDING: B1 (round 2) - sc-shaft is specified as a client
component seeding useState from manualStart while reading its scenario from an
async GET. Owned by test-runner: c-1-2 goes red at step 6 on the async reading
and the Builder cannot edit the test, so the loop closes it. The residual the
loop misses is the first-frame flash, which no testid is reserved for.

*** THE ONE THING TO EYEBALL AT STEP 6 - W2 ***
The grading value of the B1 fix now rests on the ELEMENT ORDER INSIDE `calls` in
data/scenarios.json - floor 6 before floor 2 in both-sides, floor 5 before floor
8 in overtake. That order lives in spec.md prose only; c-1-1 pins the scenario
order and the keys, not the call order. Tidying the seed file back into
registration order leaves all twelve criteria green BY CONSTRUCTION and silently
reopens B1. The fix relocated the fragility rather than removing it. Filed worth
a look, not blocking, because the Builder is not guessing - the spec states and
defends the order - but read the seed file at Gate 2 and do not let anyone
normalise it.

SHIPS AS WRITTEN unless a later round changes it - 12 worth-a-look findings,
most owned by 'nothing'. The ones with teeth:
  W4 - spec.md forbids `step` deriving movement from Math.sign(target - floor),
       and a cut written that way passes all twelve criteria including the tick-5
       down row. The prohibition is ungraded. The Breaker looked for an owner and
       declined to name code-check, which is a fixed registry that cannot see it.
  W3 - the cut-calls-ahead note claims the tick-2 row grades both halves of the
       cut; it grades one. The ordering half is graded only by c-2-1, whose cuts
       list does not name cut-calls-ahead.
  W6 - cut-dispatch-target's `ahead`-empty reversal branch is unreachable on all
       five fixtures, so a third of a 7.7-minute cut is dead ungraded code.
  W7 - three skeleton locals are unused once the cuts are open. Owner typecheck,
       which is FAIL-OPEN. It is worth-a-look rather than blocking, so the gate
       correctly did not add a verify_later entry - but someone should still read
       typecheck_fail_open in skeleton-check.json at step 8.
  W1 - the seed reorder made /scenarios/overtake open its doors on an empty
       landing on the manual walk. Ungraded, live session-1 route, pack-writer.
  W11 - the idea's payoff was a visible trace; the spec ships JSON only.
  W12 - session 1's largest cut is 58% of its cut minutes, which the share check
        structurally skips at two cuts. Six consecutive projects have overrun.

WHY 12 WORTH-A-LOOK AND NOT 7: the Breaker deliberately restated round 1's seven
kept findings so the approved record does not lose them. That is the round-memory
fix working, and gate1-check confirms drift 0 - nothing re-raised more harshly,
no owner moved to 'nothing'.

gate2.note:
GATE 2 APPROVED. Human decision, read from results.json and mutation.json rather
than by hand-testing - which is what this gate exists to replace.

CRITERIA: 12 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip, 0 missing, in 45.2 seconds. Builder retries
used: ZERO - the code passed the whole suite on its first attempt, against tests
it could not edit. code_checks declared none, as the spec states (nothing in this
project reads a clock; a tick is a tick, never a second).

MUTATION - leave-one-out, ok, checked 5 of 5, ungraded [], inconclusive []:
  cut-calls-ahead      red: c-2-2                              stayed green: -
  cut-dispatch-target  red: c-2-1 c-2-2 c-2-3                  stayed green: -
  cut-run-until        red: c-2-1 c-2-2 c-2-3 c-2-4 c-2-6      stayed green: -
  cut-step-doors       red: c-1-5                              stayed green: -
  cut-step-move        red: c-1-3 c-1-4 c-1-5                  stayed green: -
Nothing stayed green anywhere. Every one of the five student tasks turns at least
one of its own criteria red when it alone is removed, so no task can be skipped
while the suite still reads green. `checked 5 of 5` is recorded deliberately: the
check is narrowable with --only/--max, so ok:true over a subset would prove
nothing about a task that was skipped.

*** W2 HAND-CHECK - the item Gate 1 carried here, and the one no script can do ***
Read app/data/scenarios.json directly:
  both-sides  calls in file order: [(6,0), (2,0)]   spec requires 6 before 2  OK
  overtake    calls in file order: [(5,2), (8,0)]   spec requires 5 before 8  OK
The seed order survived the build, so round 1's B1 fix is still biting. THE
FRAGILITY IS UNCHANGED: no criterion pins that element order, so anyone tidying
the file into registration order would keep all twelve criteria green and
silently un-grade both the direction filter and the tie rule. Carry this to
Gate 3 and into any feedback round. Do not let the seed file be normalised.

ROUND-2 B1, the only blocking finding at Gate 1, was owned by test-runner and the
loop closed it as predicted: the shaft page is built and c-1-2 passes. The
residual the loop cannot reach is the first-frame flash, for which no testid is
reserved - unchanged, still ungraded, still not blocking.

STILL OPEN, all recorded at Gate 1 as worth-a-look and none of them fixed here:
  W4  spec.md forbids `step` deriving movement from Math.sign(target - floor);
      a cut written that way passes all twelve criteria including the tick-5
      down row, so the prohibition remains ungraded by anything.
  W7  three skeleton locals are unused once the cuts are open. Owner typecheck,
      which is FAIL-OPEN - read typecheck_fail_open in skeleton-check.json at
      step 10 and require it false. It is not in verify_later because W7 is
      worth-a-look, not blocking, and only blocking findings carry that
      obligation.
  W6  cut-dispatch-target's `ahead`-empty reversal branch is unreachable on all
      five fixtures - dead, ungraded code inside a 7.7-minute cut.
  W1  /scenarios/overtake now opens its doors on an empty landing on the manual
      walk, after the seed reorder. Live session-1 route, ungraded, pack-writer.
  W10 shaft DOM order is unpinned, so an upside-down shaft satisfies c-1-2.
  W11 the idea's payoff was a visible trace; the spec ships JSON only.
  W12 session 1's largest cut is 58% of its cut minutes, which the share check
      structurally skips at two cuts. Six consecutive projects have overrun, so
      expect the pack to disclose an overrun and name real trims.

gate3.note:
GATE 3 APPROVED. Human decision. Gate 3's question is whether someone could teach
a session from the guide alone, without opening the finished code - and step 13
answered it for session 1 with evidence rather than opinion.

DRY RUN: session 1, 40 minutes, taught by Priya, taught_without_the_code TRUE,
"Priya and the students were able to understand the session."

*** CORRECTION TO THE GATE 2 NOTE - read this instead of that ***
My Gate 2 note said "code_checks declared none, as the spec states". That is
FALSE and the reasoning was inverted. spec.json declares code_checks
["utc-dates"], and results.json records it ran with ok true, 0 violations. The
spec's rule that nothing in this project reads a clock is the REASON the check
exists, not a reason none was needed. The Gate 2 record is left as written rather
than rewritten, so the audit trail stays honest; this is the correction.
Found by the Pack Writer, which checked the claim against results.json instead of
believing the note it was given.

WHAT THE 40 MINUTES DOES NOT SETTLE. The pack timed session 1 at 47 and said it
reaches 40 ONLY by taking spec.md's own drop candidate - handing cut-step-doors
over already written, which saves 11 and costs c-1-5, the only session-1
criterion grading that cut. Priya measured 40 and the note does not say which
happened:
  (a) the trim was taken, so students did not type cut-step-doors in session 1
      (still graded by session 2's folds, per W8), or
  (b) it fit without the trim, and the pack's estimate was 7 minutes pessimistic.
Those have different consequences for the next instructor. Whoever teaches it
next should record which.

SESSION 2 WAS NOT DRY-RUN, and it is the harder half: timed at 48 against 36.5
estimated, needing three trims to reach 40.5, and its heavy cut (cut-run-until)
timed at 12 minutes against 6.8 charged. _gate_blockers(st, 3) does not require
both sessions, and state.json's dry_run is a single object, so recording session 2
would have overwritten session 1's measurement - which is why session 1's numbers
are written out above. Approved on one session deliberately; run session 2 before
this is taught for real.

HANDOVER CHECKERS, read rather than assumed:
  cut              5 cuts, 0 retries
  leak-scan        ok - leaks [] AND history_leaks [] - both halves clean
  guide-lint       ok - 0 errors, 2 G032 warnings, the intended overrun disclosures
  skeleton-check   ok, typecheck_fail_open FALSE - tsc genuinely ran, so W7's
                   fail-open owner did not pass by not running
  skeleton-results 4 pass / 8 fail - the 4 passes are the no-cut criteria the spec
                   designed to survive an open skeleton; the 8 failures are every
                   criterion whose cut was removed
  deploy           ok, fresh copy + install + build + real HTTP answer, no failed
                   steps, preview server not left listening
  criteria         12 of 12 green at step 7 with ZERO builder retries; mutation ok,
                   checked 5 of 5, nothing ungraded, nothing inconclusive, nothing
                   stayed green on any of the five leave-one-out runs

THE TIMING PREDICTION CAME TRUE, AND NAMED ITS OWN CAUSE. Both sessions overrun -
47 and 48 - the seventh consecutive project. ambiguity.md W12 predicted this at
Gate 1 before any code existed and gave the structural reason: spec_linter's
45%-largest-cut rule (W114) cannot fire on a two-cut session, so cut-step-move at
58% of session 1's cut minutes raised no warning. It then timed at 12 live minutes
against 8.3 charged. The ambiguity check found a hole in the linter's coverage by
reading the spec.

PIPELINE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED THIS ROUND: guide_linter took max() over every
"N minutes" in a session file, so any larger duration mentioned anywhere became
the session's stated time. tip-split reads "40 minutes as planned below. The
honest total for the material is 45" and was scored 45; test-05's Guide Writer had
to reword a sentence to work around it. Now read from the `**Time:**` line - the
first duration on it, since the line reads "the plan runs to 47 minutes against a
40-minute cap". Falls back to the old guess with a new G033 warning when there is
no Time line, so the guess is visible. Verified across all five packs: 47, 46, 40,
40, 40 - tip-split corrected from 45 to 40. selftest 408 -> 414.

STILL OPEN AND SHIPPING, all recorded at Gate 1:
  W2  the element order inside each `calls` array in data/scenarios.json is
      load-bearing and pinned by no criterion. Hand-checked at Gate 2 and intact
      (both-sides 6 then 2; overtake 5 then 8). Normalising that file into
      registration order leaves all twelve criteria green and silently stops
      grading both the direction filter and the tie rule. In the pack README under
      its own heading and repeated in troubleshooting.md. DO NOT NORMALISE IT.
  W4  the prohibition on `step` deriving movement from Math.sign(target - floor)
      passes all twelve criteria. Owned by nothing; the guide teaches it and says
      plainly that no test catches it.
  W6  cut-dispatch-target's ahead-empty reversal branch never executes on any of
      the five fixtures - the guide says to write it and not to spend minutes
      justifying it.
  W1  /scenarios/overtake opens its doors on an empty landing on the manual walk
      after the seed reorder. Explained in README, session-1.md and troubleshooting.
  W10 shaft DOM order and the tick readout past 0 are ungraded.
  W11 the idea's payoff was a visible trace; the spec ships JSON only - the pack
      writes out the devtools fetch and console.table with both expected tables.
